security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, when an IOPMP driver writes ENTRY_CFG with r=1 (data read only) on hardware where HWCFG3.xinr=1, the driver assumes x permission is independently denied, but the hardware merges instruction-fetch into data-read — effectively granting r+x access to DMA initiators without the kernel's awareness.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: IOPMP ENTRY_CFG write path that sets r permission bits without first reading HWCFG3.xinr to determine whether x bits are independently enforced; also any code that assumes SRCMD_X/SRCMD_XH are writable and meaningful when xinr=1
security_spec.summary: HWCFG3.xinr=1 collapses instruction-fetch into data-read permission, so a kernel IOPMP driver setting r=1/x=0 silently grants execute access to DMA-capable peripherals on data-only buses.

findings.finding: These are clock gate definitions for IOPMP-related clock domains (CLK_IOPMP_VOSYS_DPU_PCLK etc.). They are purely infrastructure clock enables and do not touch any IOPMP ENTRY_CFG register, HWCFG3, or SRCMD_X/SRCMD_XH fields. They are unrelated to the described vulnerability pattern.
